_comment: The mirror of sca-not-required: same shape, same readable shipped XPI, but the archive's authored source is TypeScript. The shipped background.js is the COMPILED output, so no file in the archive is byte-identical to it and sca-not-required must NOT fire - a build ran, and the archive is what the reviewer needs. types.d.ts is the negative control: types-only, emits nothing. Because the review stays SCA, the source tree IS reviewed: background.ts is the review target and the XPI is the shipped sibling. What proves the mode in the golden is the "Build process review" step - undeclared-build-source is input: sca, so it can only appear in a kept SCA review.
